column1: # Stress turns: 30 turns written to break the rule, after it was frozen (git tag frozen-v1).
# Written by the AI assistant that also built the rule, so they are not independent evidence
# and not a sample of real candidates. They are the hard cases it could think of:
#   A  questions that are not phrased as questions
#   B  answers that sound like questions
#   C  thinking aloud that sounds like a question or an answer
#   D  turns that are an answer and a check at once (marked unsure: TurnCheck should ask)
# Run once, with no change to the prompts, the wording check, the graph or the sheets:
#     python3 replay/replay.py turns replay/stress-turns.tsv
# The counts say where TurnCheck breaks, not how often it would with real candidates.
# One turn per line:    question number | what was meant | the turn | the sheet entry a question should get
# A  questions that are not phrased as questions
4 | question | I'm assuming the duplicates are exact copies | 4.1
5 | question | I'd need to know which tool runs the pipeline | 5.1
1 | question | tell me what incremental means here | 1.2
1 | question | I was wondering if I can answer with Spark | c.tools
3 | question | sorry, I didn't catch the second part | c.repeat
4 | question | before I answer, which warehouse is this on | 4.3
4 | question | it depends whether you mean in the stream or after loading | 4.2
3 | question | I don't know how much detail you want | c.length
2 | question | a hint would help here | c.check
1 | question | so by model you mean a SQL file | 1.3
# B  answers that sound like questions
1 | answer | what I'd do is set it to incremental and only pick up rows newer than the last run
4 | answer | how I'd do it is keep the first row for each event id and drop the rest
2 | answer | when a value changes you close the old row and add a new one with new dates
5 | answer | why it failed is the first thing, so I'd read the error in the scheduler log
4 | answer | do a merge on the event id so a second copy never gets inserted
1 | answer | can't remember the exact syntax but you filter on a timestamp inside an incremental block
2 | answer | would be type 2 for me, a new row for every change with valid from and valid to
5 | answer | is the upstream file there, that's what I'd check first, because most failures are missing data
# C  thinking aloud that sounds like a question or an answer
1 | thinking | what's the word for it
3 | thinking | how do I put this
5 | thinking | where would I even start
4 | thinking | I'd probably, hmm
2 | thinking | so you'd take the old row and, no wait
1 | thinking | is it incremental, is it, um
# D  an answer and a check at once
2 | unsure | type 2, right
4 | unsure | keep the latest one per event id, or is that not what you mean
1 | unsure | I'd filter on the updated timestamp, does that make sense
3 | unsure | star is the simpler one, isn't it
5 | unsure | check the logs first, I guess, is that what you're after
4 | unsure | you'd dedupe on the id, I think, if they really are exact copies
